title: Confession and Will
premise: Zephyrine Yarrow, the reclusive archivist of Saint Aldhelm's Cathedral, is paid a retainer by a dying magistrate to prove that a murder scheduled to occur in the locked crypt will not happen — a crime foretold in a confession letter dated three weeks in the future. As Zephyrine investigates, he discovers the 'dead' witness at the heart of the confession is alive, hidden among the cathedral's own found family of misfits and clerics, and that the magistrate's payment was itself an act of loyalty meant to shield the killer. When the statute expires on the night of the winter solstice service, Zephyrine must choose between exposing the truth that will destroy the people he loves or burying the confession forever. He chooses truth — but delivers it in a way that saves both the witness and the killer's soul, ending with the crypt unlocked for the first time in forty years.
about_author: Hazel Crane is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing centuries of confessions, wills, and burial registers before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries from a converted vestry office, where she still keeps one drawer locked, just in case.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Zephyrine Yarrow's POV. A gaunt stranger arrives at the archive office and pays a year's fee in advance: prove that no murder has occurred in the cathedral crypt — yet. Zephyrine, who values invisibility above all, almost refuses until he recognizes the magistrate's seal. The beat is unease masked as professional detachment.

chapters.title: A Confession Dated Forward
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In the sealed records he finds a confession letter describing a killing in the crypt, dated three weeks hence, signed by someone long registered as dead. The emotional beat is vertigo — his ordered world of paper suddenly runs ahead of time itself.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, with a brief interlude from the verger, Tomasin. They inspect the crypt together; the lock is intact, the dust undisturbed, but a fresh candle stub burns where none should be. Tomasin lies about the key. The beat is the first crack in trust.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He interviews the cathedral's tight circle — organist, sacristan, the canon — and every one of them repeats the same phrase about the witness, Mirabel Quill: she died years ago. The identical wording feels rehearsed. The beat is creeping suspicion of complicity.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Tracing the retainer money, he learns the magistrate, Lord Aldery, is terminally ill and made the payment through an intermediary — his own estranged daughter. Why would a dying man buy proof of a murder not yet committed? The beat is dread deepening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Found Family
chapters.summary: Tomasin's POV. A warm chapter showing the cathedral community that took Zephyrine in when he had nothing: shared suppers, choir practice, small kindnesses. Tomasin watches Zephyrine asking questions and quietly warns the others. The beat is tenderness shadowed by protective secrecy.

chapters.title: What the Register Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Forensic reading of the burial register reveals Mirabel Quill's death entry was added in different ink, decades after the fact. Someone falsified her death — kindly or cruelly, he can't tell. The beat is the thrill of the hunt curdling into guilt.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Will
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He obtains a copy of Lord Aldery's will: everything goes to charity except a sealed codicil 'to be opened upon proof.' The payment wasn't for prevention — it was a condition. The beat is betrayal; Zephyrine realizes he's a clause in someone's testament.

chapters.title: Choir of Denials
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Confronting the sacristan privately, he gets half a story: Mirabel witnessed something terrible forty years ago inside the crypt and was hidden rather than silenced. The sacristan begs him to stop before the statute expires. The beat is sympathy warring with duty.

chapters.title: Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Someone ransacks the archive overnight, burning loose papers but leaving the confession untouched — a message, not a theft. Zephyrine begins sleeping in the archive. The beat is fear arriving at his doorstep, and a stubborn refusal to leave.

chapters.title: The Daughter's Bargain
chapters.summary: Interleaved POV: Aldery's daughter, Vesper. She confesses to the reader (not Zephyrine) that she delivered the retainer knowing what it would set in motion, torn between loyalty to her father's plan and horror at its cost. The beat is tragic complicity.

chapters.title: A Life Among Ledgers
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, reflective midpoint. Flashbacks to how he became invisible: a childhood erased by scandal, saved by the cathedral's embrace. He understands now why the circle protects Mirabel — because they once protected him the same way. The beat is painful self-recognition.

chapters.title: The Second Key
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He discovers the crypt has a second entrance through the ossuary passage, and evidence someone has used it recently — small footprints, wax drippings forming a trail. The witness may be living beneath their feet. The beat is breathless hope.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Legal research shows the original crime becomes unprosecutable in nine days — unless a related felony occurred. Whoever scheduled the future murder needs it done before the deadline, or never. The clock becomes the antagonist. The beat is accelerating pressure.

chapters.title: Vigil
chapters.summary: Tomasin's POV. Tomasin keeps a secret vigil at the ossuary door and is caught by Zephyrine. Cornered, he admits Mirabel is alive, frail, and hiding by choice — and that the 'future murder' in the confession is her own planned death, volunteered to close the case forever. The beat is heartbreak.

chapters.title: Confession and Will
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He reads the full confession at last: forty years ago Mirabel saw the then-young Lord Aldery kill a man in the crypt; her planned death would expire the statute and free them all. The title chapter lands the moral crisis: loyalty asks him to let it happen. The beat is the weight of choice.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided — Zephyrine, Vesper, Tomasin. The cathedral fills for the solstice service while below, preparations for Mirabel's final night proceed. Vesper breaks, racing to warn Zephyrine. The beat is converging threads, tension at breaking point.

chapters.title: The Unlocked Door
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He descends into the crypt during the service and finds Mirabel alive, dignified, ready. Instead of stopping her by force, he offers a third path: testimony recorded and sealed, released only after the statute lapses — truth preserved, vengeance forgone. The beat is quiet heroism.

chapters.title: What the Bell Heard
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, her only chapter. She tells her own story of the night forty years ago, the terror, the kindness of strangers who buried her name to save her life. She accepts Zephyrine's bargain. The beat is release after a lifetime of silence.

chapters.title: Proof of No Murder
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He delivers his report to the dying Lord Aldery: no murder has occurred, none will, and the statute has expired. Aldery weeps — his payment was penance, hoping someone would find the courage he lacked. The beat is catharsis and forgiveness.

chapters.title: Codicil Opened
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The will's codicil funds a home for witnesses in hiding, endowed anonymously — Aldery's final act of repair. Vesper reconciles with her father's memory; Tomasin forgives himself. The beat is grief transmuted into legacy.

chapters.title: The Archive, After
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, epilogue. Spring: the crypt stands unlocked, Mirabel tends roses above it under her true name, and Zephyrine files the sealed testimony in a drawer he no longer locks. Invisibility, he reflects, was never really an option — nor, anymore, a wish. The beat is belonging earned through truth.
